textbookText: Parapodia: Locomotory organ of Nereis. Appendages: Lateral outgrowths arising from body. Example: legs, tentacles, antennae etc. Muscular feet: Locomotory organs of molluscs. For example: apple snail (Pila), garden snail (Helix) etc. Tube feet: Locomotory organ of echinodermata. Example: Starfish, Sea cucumber etc. Fins: Locomotory organ of fishes. Limbs: Locomotory organs of tetrapods such as amphibians, reptiles, aves and mammals. Holozoic nutrition: Mode of nutrition in organisms in which they engulf solid or liquid food which is not prepared by them as found in green plants. Holophytic nutrition: Mode of nutrition in organisms in which they prepare food themselves. Mixotrophic nutrition: Organism showing both autotrophic and heterotrophic nutrition. Example: Euglena Saprotrophic: Organisms feeding on dead and decaying organic matters, Intracellular digestion: Digestion takes place inside the cell. Extracellular digestion: Digestion takes place outside the cell i.e in alimentary canal. Anaerobic respirartion: Respiration which takes place in the absence of oxygen. Aerobic respiration: Respiration which takes place in the presence of oxygen. External gills: Gills on the outer body surface but not enclosed by body wall. Example: amphibian larva and some larval fishes. Internal gills: Gills inside the body developed as pharyngeal outgrowth. Tracheae: Respiratory organ in the body of some arthropods. Example: insects Book lungs: Respiratory organ in some arthropods such as spider and scorpion Pulmonary sac: Respiratory organ of terrestrial molluscs. Example: Pila Open circulation: Blood remains in blood sinuses or cavities, there is no veins and capillaries. Closed circulation: Blood flows within blood vessels. Myogenic heart: Heartbeat originates from specialized nodule tissue of heart itself. Neurogenic heart: Heart beat originates from a nervous tissue situated near the heart. Contractile vacuole: Osmoregulatory organelle in protozoans. Flame cells: Excretory organs of platyhelminthes. Nephridia: Excretory organ in phylum annelida. Malpighian tubules: Excretory organ in most of the insects. Green gland or coxal glands: Excretory organs of crustaceans. Organ of Bojanus: Excretory organ of mollusca. Monoecious/hermaphrodite/bisexual: Both male and female sex organ present in the same body. Unisexual/dioecious: Male and female are separate. Oviparous: Egg laying animals Viviparous: Animals giving direct birth to the young Ovoviviparous: Animal giving birth to immature youngones. Sexual dimorphism: Condition in which male and female are distinct by their morphology. Protandry: Condition in which male reproductive organ mature earlier than female reproductive organ. Example: Earthworm Biology, Grade 11 | 320

Protogyny: Female reproductive organ matures earlier than male reproductive organ. Example: Human External fertilization: Fertilization takes place outside the body of female. Internal fertilization: Fertilization takes place inside the body of female. Direct development: No larva in the life cycle Indirect development: Larval stages in the life cycle Retogressive metamorphosis: Larva is more advanced than adult.Example: Herdmania Ureotelic animal: An animal which excretes urea as chief nitrogenous waste. Human, frog etc. Uricotelic animal: An animal which excretes uric acid as chief nitrogenous waste. Bird, land reptiles etc. Ammonotelic animal: An animal which excretes ammonia as chief nitrogenous waste. Freshwater bony fishes, tadpole etc. Aminotelic animal: An animal which excretes excess amino acid. Starfish,Unio 8.2.2 PHYLUM PORIFERA The name porifera (L; porus-pore; ferro-to bear) was coined by Robert grant. The evidence of their animal nature was given by John Ellis in 1765 in which he found water currents. Porifera are commonly called sponges. Branch of biology which deals with the study of porifera is called parazoology.
1. Porifera are all aquatic animals, which are mostly found in marine water and few of them are found in freshwater.
2. They are primitive and first multicellular organisms having cellular grade of body organization.

3. Adult body is sessile and sedentary, found attached on substratum. 4. Body shape is vase or cylinder like, tubular, cushion like, branched tube like. 5. Their body is either asymmetrical or radially symmetrical. 6. They are diploblastic i.e. developed from two germ layers in embryonic stage. Their

body wall consists of outer pinacoderm (dermal epithelium) and inner choanoderm (gastral epithelium) with non-cellular gelationous mesenchyme layer in between. Mesenchyme is composed of skeletal elements and amoeboid cells. 7. Body is perforated by many pores where smaller pores are called ostia and larger pores are called oscula.
